raw: You can activate your new card in the app under Cards → Activate, either by tapping the card against your phone or by scanning it with the camera. The app never asks you to type the full card number or PIN to activate. If you want to use the card before it is activated, you can already add it to Apple Pay or Google Pay.

Chinor Bank accounts are available to residents aged 16 or over of one of our 12 supported countries. You will need a passport or national ID card and a short selfie video to verify your identity in the app.

You can use any ATM that accepts your card network. Withdrawals are free up to 2,500,000 UZS per month on Standard and 6,000,000 UZS on Plus; above that a 1.3 % fee applies, and some ATM operators add their own surcharge, shown on screen before you confirm. ATMs with no operator surcharge are marked in the app under Cards → ATMs near me.

You can set up automatic top-up in the app under Account → Auto top-up. Choose a balance threshold and an amount of at least 50,000 UZS; when your balance falls below the threshold, the top-up is taken from your linked card. Debit-card top-ups are free; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee.

Cash deposited at a Chinor ATM is credited immediately, and cash deposited at a branch counter is credited by the end of the same business day. Chinor does not accept cheques, so a cheque cannot be credited. If a cash deposit is still missing after that time, a human agent can check it with the deposit receipt.

A failed transfer is returned to your balance within 2 business days, and the app shows the reason — most often wrong recipient details, a limit, sanctions screening or insufficient balance. Correct the details and send it again; if it fails again for no shown reason, a human agent can check it.

A domestic transfer can be cancelled in the app only while its status is Scheduled; once it shows Sent it cannot be cancelled. An international (SWIFT) transfer can be recalled within 24 hours of sending for a 90,000 UZS recall fee, but recall is not guaranteed because the receiving bank must agree.

A replacement card is sent automatically, free of charge, 45 days before your card expires, to the address in your profile. Your current card keeps working until the last day of its expiry month. When the new card arrives, activate it in the app under Cards → Activate.

Chinor cards work in more than 180 countries wherever the Visa or Mastercard network is accepted, except in countries under international sanctions. If a merchant declines the card, the app shows the decline reason under the transaction.

Standard delivery takes 7 business days. Express delivery takes 2 business days and costs 45,000 UZS. The first physical card has no delivery fee on either plan.

You can link a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card issued in your own name under Account → Top up → Add card, and use it for manual or automatic top-ups. Debit-card top-ups are free; credit-card top-ups carry a 1.1 % fee.

Please check in the app that the card is activated and not frozen, that the relevant toggle under Cards → Security (contactless, online, ATM, magnetic stripe) is switched on, and that your daily limit has not been reached. If a chip card fails at every terminal it is treated as damaged and replaced free of charge.

First check the merchant's trading name and location under the transaction in the app — it can differ from the shop name. If you still do not recognise it, freeze the card in the app and raise a dispute from the transaction screen (Transaction → Something wrong → Dispute) within 60 days of the statement date.

Chinor converts at the interbank mid-market rate, plus a 0.9 % weekend markup from Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 and a 0.6 % fee above the Standard monthly allowance. If the merchant offered to charge you in your home currency and you accepted, the merchant's own rate applied (dynamic currency conversion), which Chinor cannot refund; always choose to pay in the local currency.

Please check the ATM location and time under the transaction in the app. If you did not make the withdrawal, freeze the card immediately, call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22, and raise a dispute from the transaction screen within 60 days of the statement date.
You can view or change your 4-digit PIN in the app under Cards → Security → PIN after confirming your passcode and biometrics. There is no fee, and the new PIN works from the next chip transaction.

Freeze the card now in the app under Cards → Freeze (or call the 24-hour card line +998 (71) 000-11-22), then cancel it and order a replacement; the first replacement each calendar year is free. Dispute any transaction you do not recognise from the transaction screen within 60 days of the statement date.

Chinor accounts are available to residents of 12 countries: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkey, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Germany, Poland, the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom. Cards can be used in more than 180 countries, except those under international sanctions.

The decline reason is shown under the transaction in the app. Common causes are insufficient balance in the payment currency, a frozen card, a blocked merchant category or toggle under Cards → Security, the daily limit, the merchant not completing 3-D Secure, or a fraud-monitoring check that asks you to confirm the payment in the app.

A withdrawal is usually declined because the 6,000,000 UZS daily ATM limit was reached, ATM withdrawals are switched off under Cards → Security, the PIN was wrong, the ATM does not support your card network, or the ATM is out of cash. The reason is shown under the attempt in the app.

Go to Cards → New virtual card in the app and choose Disposable. It is created instantly and free on both plans; the details regenerate after each payment, and you can create up to 6 per day with a maximum of 3,000,000 UZS per payment.

Phone number, email and address are changed in the app under Profile → Personal details and take effect immediately; a new address is confirmed with a one-time code sent to your registered phone. A legal name change requires uploading the new document and is processed within 3 business days.

Exchange is free up to 15,000,000 UZS equivalent per month on Standard and unlimited on Plus; above the Standard allowance a 0.6 % fee applies. From Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 a 0.9 % weekend markup is added because markets are closed.

Chinor uses the interbank mid-market rate during market hours, with a 0.9 % markup at weekends (Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59). The live rate for any of our 14 supported currencies is shown in the app under Exchange before you confirm; I cannot quote a live rate here.

Open Exchange in the app, choose the currency pair and amount, and confirm — the balance is converted instantly at the interbank mid-market rate. You can hold 14 currencies, and exchange is free up to 15,000,000 UZS per month on Standard.

Every fee appears as a separate line under the transaction in the app. The possible fees are the 0.9 % weekend markup, the 0.6 % fee above the exchange allowance, the 0.5 % fee at gambling or money-transfer merchants, the 1.3 % fee above the free ATM allowance, the 1.1 % credit-card top-up fee, and the 25,000 UZS Plus subscription. If the fee line does not match any of these, a human agent can review it.

Tap Forgot passcode on the app login screen. You will record a new selfie video, which is matched against your verified identity document, and then set a new 6-digit passcode; the reset takes effect immediately. I cannot reset or see your passcode.

After 3 wrong attempts the PIN is blocked. Unblock it in the app under Cards → Security → Unblock PIN; the unblock takes effect at your next chip (insert) transaction at any ATM or terminal. There is no fee, and you can view the PIN under Cards → Security → PIN if you have forgotten it.

For a domestic transfer the sender needs your 20-digit Chinor account number and the bank code 00099. For an international transfer they need your account number, the bank name (Chinor Bank, Tashkent) and the BIC CHNRUZTA; international payments are credited within 1 business day of reaching us. You can find these details in the app under Account → Details.

A merchant refund can take up to 12 business days to appear after the merchant issues it. Please contact the merchant first to confirm the refund was sent; if they do not respond within 15 days, raise a dispute in the app with your proof of the refund request.

A reverted card payment is usually a pre-authorisation — for example at a hotel, fuel pump or car rental — that the merchant did not settle, so the reserved amount was released back to your balance. Pre-authorisations are released automatically after 9 business days at the latest.

You can request closure in the app under Profile → Close account. Your balance must be zero and there must be no pending transactions or open disputes; closure is completed within 14 days, and your statements stay downloadable from the web portal for 5 years.

The decline reason is shown under the transaction in the app. Common causes are insufficient balance in the payment currency, a frozen card, a blocked merchant category or toggle under Cards → Security, the daily limit, the merchant not completing 3-D Secure, or a fraud-monitoring check that asks you to confirm the payment in the app.

Exchange is free up to 15,000,000 UZS equivalent per month on Standard and unlimited on Plus; above the Standard allowance a 0.6 % fee applies. From Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 a 0.9 % weekend markup is added because markets are closed.

Every fee appears as a separate line under the transaction in the app. The possible fees are the 0.9 % weekend markup, the 0.6 % fee above the exchange allowance, the 0.5 % fee at gambling or money-transfer merchants, the 1.3 % fee above the free ATM allowance, the 1.1 % credit-card top-up fee, and the 25,000 UZS Plus subscription. If the fee line does not match any of these, a human agent can review it.
Top-ups from a debit card are free. Top-ups from a credit card carry a 1.1 % fee, shown before you confirm. The card must be a Visa, Mastercard, UzCard or Humo card in your own name.

Card top-ups are normally instant but can take up to 2 business days when the card issuer holds them; bank-transfer top-ups are credited within 1 business day. If the time has passed, ask your card issuer or bank whether the payment left, and a human agent can trace it with the reference.

A spare (second) physical card is included in the Chinor Plus plan. On Standard, an additional physical card beyond the plan allowance costs 35,000 UZS. Order it under Cards → Order card; delivery takes 7 business days.

Top-up limits are 30,000,000 UZS per day and 100,000,000 UZS per month. Single top-ups above 10,000,000 UZS, or total deposits above 50,000,000 UZS in a month, may require proof of the source of funds, which you upload in the app within 10 days.

Chinor Bank accounts are available to residents aged 16 or over of one of our 12 supported countries. You will need a passport or national ID card and a short selfie video to verify your identity in the app.

Identity verification is usually completed within 2 hours and at most 1 business day. It takes a passport or national ID card and a selfie video, and is required by anti-money-laundering law before an account can be used.
You can dispute a transaction in the app under Transactions → Dispute. The deadline is 60 days from the statement date, and a human agent in in-app chat can help with the process.
A direct debit is taken within the amount and time frame stated by the merchant. The merchant cannot take more than that, and if they do, you can dispute the extra amount as an overcharge.
The daily ATM limit is 2,500,000 UZS and the weekly limit is 10,000,000 UZS. Some ATM networks also have their own daily limits, so the ATM might decline if you try to withdraw more than that.
